_comment: Config for the LLM control panel + router. Edit freely, then reload the web page (panel picks up changes live, except the 'server' block which needs a panel restart). Remote API keys do NOT live here — they go in secrets.json (chmod 600), referenced by 'key_ref'.

estimator._comment: VRAM_gb(ctx,kv) = base_gb + per_1k_gb * ctx/1000, plus mtp_overhead_gb when MTP is on, plus (this model's file size - base_weight_gb). Refit 2026-09-04 against the sm120 build from clean measurements: q4_0 and q8_0 are exact to ~0.01 GB over 32k-196k; f16 is DERIVED from the q4_0/q8_0 KV slopes, not measured (f16 OOMs past ~32k anyway). NOTE the fit models VRAM AT LOAD. Real failures happen at PEAK during a long prompt, which grows with context: q8_0/80k/MTP loads at 15.24 GB and dies, while Q4_K_S/8k loads at 15.31 GB and is fine. No single cap separates those, so the shipped presets carry MEASURED vram_gb and the fit is only used for the custom-preset builder.
estimator._mtp_comment: Extra VRAM when speculative decoding is on (spec_type=draft-mtp): the NextN draft head plus its own draft KV. Same linear form as coeffs_gb: gb = 0.75 + 0.0039 * ctx/1000. Measured on the RTX 5080 at IQ3_XXS and identical for q4_0 and q8_0 KV: +900 MiB @32k, +1030 MiB @64k. Added on top of coeffs_gb only when MTP is enabled. NOTE this figure bundles the base model's own head weights (see mtp_head_gb) with the draft KV, because it was measured as a difference on a GGUF that has the head embedded.
estimator._slot_comment: Cost of EACH server slot beyond the first: gb = (slots-1) * 0.4385. CONSTANT, not ctx-scaled — measured 1346 MiB for 3 extra slots at BOTH 32k and 96k (IQ3_XXS/q4_0/MTP2): 32k 13020 -> 14366 MiB, 96k 13646 -> 14992 MiB. The linear form is kept for symmetry with coeffs_gb; the slope is genuinely 0. llama.cpp's --parallel defaults to -1 = auto, which server.cpp forces to n_parallel=4 + kv_unified=true (tools/server/server.cpp:152) — so 'auto' is ALWAYS 4 slots, and an explicit --no-kv-unified cannot take effect under auto because that assignment runs after arg parsing. Unified KV shares one pool of -c tokens, so the KV term is NOT multiplied; with kv_unified off llama.cpp instead splits it (llama-context.cpp:293: n_ctx_seq = n_ctx / n_seq_max), so the KV term is not multiplied there either — only this per-slot constant applies. COST BEYOND VRAM: unified KV is ~3x slower per stream. At 96k, 1 slot decodes 73-82 tok/s while auto/4-slot decodes 25.4 tok/s single-stream and ~7.5 x4 = 30 tok/s aggregate under 4 concurrent requests. So auto only pays off when several clients must be served at once, and even then total throughput is barely above one 1-slot stream.
estimator._vision_comment: VRAM handed back by vision: off. MEASURED, not the file size: mmproj-F16.gguf is 885 MiB but dropping it saved 1136 MiB = 1.11 GiB (96k/q4_0/MTP2/1 slot: 14782 MiB with the projector, 13646 without) because its own compute buffers go too. coeffs_gb were fit WITH the projector loaded, so this is subtracted, never added.
estimator._mtp_head_comment: Weight cost of the NextN/MTP head EMBEDDED in the main GGUF. Read out of the tensor table: 0.351 GB in Qwen3.8-27B-UD-IQ3_XXS, 0.351 in UD-IQ4_XS, 0.348 in GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-mtp -- the head keeps its own precision whatever the trunk quant is, so one constant covers the family. It is loaded ONLY when --spec-type draft-mtp is passed: common.cpp:1714 sets mparams.load_mtp from the spec type and models/qwen35.cpp then marks every nextn tensor TENSOR_SKIP when it is false. So a '-mtp' GGUF is free while MTP is off and costs this much the moment it goes on, on top of mtp_overhead_gb's draft KV. mtp_overhead_gb was measured as (on - off) on the base model and therefore already contains one copy of this, which the estimator removes before charging the model's own.
estimator._draft_archs_comment: arch -> --spec-type, for standalone draft models. Built in: eagle3, dflash, dspark (and an embedded NextN head, which needs no file). When llama.cpp gains another speculative family, add it here -- {"<general.architecture>": "draft-<x>"} -- and rescan will classify those GGUFs without any code change.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ3_XXS.label: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 125B-A6B (UD-IQ3_XXS)
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-UD-IQ3_XXS.note: 180B total params / 6B active MoE + 51B engram table. 76.3 GiB on disk - it does NOT fit in VRAM+RAM and streams from NVMe. Needs --n-cpu-moe and --lazy-mode (both live in each preset's extra_flags) and ngl=auto so --fit can size the split. MTP: the main GGUF has NO nextn tensors, so it can only come from a separate mtp-*.gguf (mtp_source: external). Both heads in the dir are UNLOADABLE on mainline b10816 — mtp-shared-* is missing token_embd.weight by design, and the non-shared mtp-Q4_K_M.gguf wants a HyperConnections output norm this build does not have; it needs Unsloth's qwen4exp/mtp fork. Measured there anyway: MTP is a ~21% NET LOSS on this card because it costs ~2.8 GB and forces n-cpu-moe 48. supports_mtp stays false; set mtp_head to one of mtp_draft_files to retry on a future build.

residency.hint: streams from disk of experts: start at --n-cpu-moe 41 with -ngl auto and a --fit-target, then sweep it

Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-GGUF-IQ3_XXS.label: Qwen3.8-27B GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS (no MTP head)
Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-GGUF-IQ3_XXS.note: HEAD-LESS build: 64 blocks, no blk.64.nextn.* in the GGUF, so --spec-type draft-mtp CANNOT run here -- llama.cpp fails the load looking for tensors that are not in the file. Ships the BF16 projector, so this is the vision half of the GSQ-RCO pair. 10.08 GB of weights, 0.85 GB lighter than UD-IQ3_XXS. Use the -mtp sibling if you want speculative decoding.

Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-GGUF-IQ3_XXS-mtp.label: Qwen3.8-27B GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS + MTP head
Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-GGUF-IQ3_XXS-mtp.note: SAME trunk as the plain GSQ-RCO build plus the NextN head in block 64 (10.43 vs 10.08 GB). TEXT ONLY -- no mmproj in the repo, so vision is off whatever a preset asks for. The head is TENSOR_SKIPped unless --spec-type draft-mtp is passed, so MTP off costs exactly what the head-less build costs; MTP on adds 0.35 GB of head plus the draft KV.

Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-GGUF-IQ3_S-mtp.label: Qwen3.8-27B GSQ-RCO IQ3_S + MTP head
Qwen3.8-27B-GSQ-RCO-GGUF-IQ3_S-mtp.note: 12.12 GB = the IQ3_S trunk plus the NextN head. Unlike the IQ3_XXS pair this one keeps the BF16 projector, so vision AND MTP are both available — but they compete for the same ~2 GB of slack, so expect to choose. Both builds live in the SAME directory, so the 'gguf' key is what separates them — without it the launcher and the panel resolve the name differently ('..._S.gguf' vs '..._S-mtp.gguf' sort one way under shell collation and the other under Python's) and could load different files.

runtime._comment: Global llama.cpp runtime knobs, passed as env to serve-vlm.sh. A preset can override any of these. Leave null/absent to use serve-vlm.sh's own default.

_notes.thinking: on = always reason (best quality, burns output tokens) | off = never (fast, best for agent tool loops) | auto = chat template decides
_notes.context_shift: off (RECOMMENDED for agents): server errors when full instead of silently dropping oldest tokens. on: keeps generating by discarding history — corrupts agent state.
_notes.cache_reuse: min chunk size (tokens) to reuse from KV cache via shifting. 256 is a good default; big speedup for agent loops that compact/edit history. 0 disables.
_notes.image_min_tokens: Qwen-VL needs >=1024 image tokens for accurate grounding. Higher = more detail, more VRAM/time.
_notes.spec_type: draft-mtp = use the MTP/NextN draft head baked into the Qwen3.8-27B GGUF (no separate draft model needed) | none = plain decoding. Needs the sm120 build; the old PTX-JIT build asserts in graph_mtp and dies. Measured: 53 -> 77 tok/s prose, 53 -> 89 tok/s code. Costs ~1 GB VRAM.
_notes.spec_n_max: Draft depth. 2 = best all-round (77 prose / 89 code); 3 favours code (70 prose / 94 code); 4 was worse on both. Re-sweep after any config change.

compaction._comment: Guidance for the HARNESS (llama.cpp does not compact for you). With context_shift off, the server errors at the limit — the harness must summarize/compact before then.
compaction._notes: Trigger compaction at ~70% of the slot's context (ctx/parallel). Reserve ~30k for reasoning output + the next tool result. Use summarization, NOT hard truncation — truncation drops the system prompt and early tool results. If parallel>1, each slot only gets ctx/parallel, so scale the trigger down.

engines._comment: Inference engines installed on this box. Only ONE can hold the GPU at a time (16GB).

vllm.label: vLLM
vllm.formats: BF16/FP16, FP8, AWQ/GPTQ 4-bit (NOT GGUF IQ-quants, no multimodal GGUF)
vllm.note: WORKING on RTX 5080 (sm_120)! Requires: flashinfer-jit-cache 0.6.18+cu130, apache-tvm-ffi==0.1.11 (0.1.12+ double-registers TVM FFI), no flashinfer-cubin, VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0, FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1, cu13 toolchain. serve-vllm.sh sets these.

ollama.label: Ollama
ollama.note: Same engine as llama.cpp, port 11434, fewer exposed flags; bundles its own CUDA. Pull a model before activating.

gen_defaults._comment: Settings the ROUTER injects when a client OMITS them. NOTE: serve-vlm.sh already applies Unsloth's thinking-aware sampling at the SERVER level. Leave these null to let the server's profile win (recommended). Set a value only to force it for every client.

sampling_reference._comment: Unsloth's recommended Qwen3-VL sampling. serve-vlm.sh picks the matching set automatically from THINKING. Shown here for reference / manual override.

thinking.note: Some users prefer temp 0.6 to curb over-long thinking.

router._comment: Point any harness at http://<box>:8001/v1 with any model id — the router forwards to whichever endpoint is active and applies gen_defaults.

endpoints.label: Local · llama.cpp (Qwen3.8-27B VLM)
endpoints.note: Runs on this RTX 5080. Uses whatever local preset is applied above.

endpoints.label: OpenRouter (many models)
endpoints.note: One key, hundreds of models. Set "openrouter" in secrets.json.

_preset_keys._comment: Every key a preset may carry, and the llama-server flag it becomes. Anything absent falls back to runtime{}, then to serve-vlm.sh's own default. The panel drops keys that do not apply to the chosen model (see drop_inapplicable) so a stale field can never reach the command line for the wrong family.
_preset_keys.ngl: -ngl, or 'auto' to omit it so --fit can size the split
_preset_keys.vision: off drops --mmproj (also forced off when the repo has no projector)
_preset_keys.spec_draft_kv: --spec-draft-type-k/-v: quantize the DRAFT context's own KV
_preset_keys.mtp_head: MTP_HEAD: embedded | auto | none | <file in the model dir> | /abs/path
_preset_keys.lazy_mode: --lazy-mode on|auto|off — on-demand rows for oversized tensors
_preset_keys.load_mode: --load-mode auto|none|mmap|mlock|mmap+mlock|dio — RAM vs disk residency; replaces the deprecated --mmap/--no-mmap/--mlock
_preset_keys.fit_target: --fit-target MiB of VRAM margin to leave free
_preset_keys.fit_ctx: --fit-ctx N floor on the context --fit may choose
_preset_keys.temp/top_p/top_k/min_p/presence_penalty/: server-level sampling. Normally LEAVE UNSET: serve-vlm.sh picks Unsloth's thinking-aware profile from `thinking`, and setting these pins one set for both modes.
_preset_keys.extra_flags: appended verbatim — last resort for anything above
_preset_keys.vram_gb: MEASURED peak. Omit it and /presets.json fills in an estimate and flags vram_measured:false so the card reads '~VRAM'.

auto_switch._comment: Client model name -> preset. When a client sends model=<alias>, the router loads that preset (its GGUF/quant, ctx, KV) if it differs from what is serving; same preset = no reload. Unmapped names are served by whatever is loaded.
